Thanks for the ping — quick first-pass notes below (keeping this high level so we can propose a targeted redline set):

1) Indemnity and liability
- FinLogic's MSA has a broad indemnity and an unlimited liability carveout for data-related claims. Recommend: cap liability at the greater of (i) total fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $2M for the pilot. Offer carveout for gross negligence or willful misconduct.

2) Data & logging
- Clause says Redwood "may" retain logs for diagnostics with no retention limit. For pilot we should propose explicit retention (30/90/180 days options) and a commitment not to use customer data to train models without consent.
- Request SOC 2 Type II report and a list of subprocessors (we can provide Redwood's SOC2 link and standard subprocessors list).

3) Residency & export controls
- FinLogic requires US residency now; flag clause that would allow global transfers. Ask for a residency guarantee for the pilot and a path to add EU residency later.

4) IP & outputs
- FinLogic's draft includes a broad ownership claim over "derivatives". We'll propose language clarifying that customer prompts and outputs remain with the customer, while Redwood retains improvements to the service and underlying models.

5) Termination & transition
- Add obligation for data return/deletion within 30 days and document export assistance for the pilot.

If you want, I can produce a tracked redline limited to the above points (1–2 pages) that keeps commercial terms intact and avoids enterprise-level escalations. Estimated turnaround: draft redline by COB tomorrow (2026-12-21) if you want the conservative option, faster if we trim scope.

Questions for sales:
- Confirm pilot billing entity (legal name, tax ID) so we can populate Order Form.
- Is FinLogic expecting any special SLAs for the pilot or credits on downtime?

I'll wait for Marissa/Kimberly to confirm and will prepare the redline accordingly.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
